doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Student stories and Mitsuyo's Motif
summary: Few return for lesson two; a clarinet student's four-note motif was named for her.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And you know but he believes me, and there have been a few people over the years that have believed what I was telling them. There was a girl that used to come and take lessons, she came the whole summer. She played the clarinet. And I gave her this idea, that, and then I told her I said, “Now I want you to come up with a four note motif.” I said, “Don’t even think about it just come up with A, anything A through G, and label it natural, sharp or whatever, and then we’ll put it together going up or down, to get to those points. And so she came up with these four notes. [scats] Something, whatever. And so for her next lesson I wrote out this four note — going through the chromatic sequence playing this motif. And her name was [sounds like] Mitsuyo. And I had it all written out for her and the title was “Mitsuyo’s Motif.” You know. So she looked at it and she was so excited you know. She was so excited that it was her name and it was perfect you know.

And boy she — when she would come for her lesson I’d have to practice a day in advance because she’d be fiddling through this — I’d have to get ready for it. But she’s the only one that I had that was that ambitious.
Well that was very astute of you to come up with that.
